Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter

## Bottom line

The package is not "fair and balanced". Read together, the Seller's update and the Disclosure Letter would let the Seller (a) leave about AUD 3.8m of known liabilities with the Company, (b) remove most of the Buyer's practical warranty protection, and (c) cap and time-limit even title and fraud-type claims. Several statements in the Seller's update are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. Use those contradictions in negotiation.

## 1. The "FINAL / market / settled at principal level" framing

- This is an assertion, not evidence. Please check our own records and with the Wattlebridge principal what was actually agreed. I can't verify it from the documents.
- Even if the headline numbers were agreed (20% cap, about 1% basket, 18 months), the agreement almost certainly covered **general warranties only**. The Seller then extends those numbers to title, capacity, tax, IP, fraud and specific indemnities. That is a structural change, not a number already agreed.
- The "market" ranges are the Seller's characterisation. They may be plausible for general warranties, but they say nothing about fundamental, tax or specific-risk protection.
- The Disclosure Letter jumps from paragraph 1.2 to 1.4. **Ask what paragraph 1.3 said and why it was removed.**

## 2. Tier 1: deal-critical issues

**A. Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m): post-Completion release is unacceptable.**
- This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. The facility must be paid out at Completion from the price, against a payout letter and simultaneous discharge of all security (PPSR, GSA and any share security).
- Change-control clause 8.1 may also trigger a default on Completion.
- The payout figure should include interest, fees and break costs.

**B. Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m, ~30% of revenue).**
- The Seller's update says the consent is "addressed". The Disclosure Letter (para 2) admits there is **no** consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- "Reasonable endeavours" plus "satisfied on delivery of written consent" would let a conditional or onerous consent count as satisfied.
- Require a condition precedent: **unconditional** written consent (or on terms acceptable to the Buyer), waivable by the Buyer only, with a walk-away right.
- Consider a retention or price adjustment as a fallback. As a rough inference, AUD 24m on about AUD 12m implied revenue is about 2x, so Bluefen represents roughly AUD 7m of value. Please sanity-check this against the model.

**C. DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) omitted from the funds flow.**
- The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller", but the liability sits in the Company, which the Buyer will own.
- Treat them as a debt-like or transaction-triggered item deducted from the price, **plus** employer on-costs (super, and payroll tax if applicable). The Seller's disclosure expressly leaves on-costs open.

**D. Ironquay IP (AUD 180,000 open, per DD-010).**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 materials passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. The risk is therefore loss of IP in the product, not just AUD 180k.
- The Seller's own letter says there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment, and that DD-010 is not bank-verified.
- Require payment before Completion (or from proceeds) and a **signed confirmatory IP assignment** (with moral rights consents) as a Completion deliverable.
- Seek a broader specific indemnity covering IP title, third-party claims and remediation cost, outside the cap, basket and disclosure.
- Verify whether other SOW fees are unpaid.

**E. DD-006 data incident.**
- About 1,240 records of personal information went to an unintended external address. The Seller's "not expected to be material" is unsupported, and its own letter says scope, access and notification are undetermined.
- The data room cut-off was 22 September and today is 5 November. If the Company is an APP entity (likely at roughly AUD 12m implied revenue, so above the small-business threshold), the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme's 30-day assessment window has probably run. Please confirm with privacy counsel.
- Demand an immediate status update: forensic findings, the NDB assessment and any OAIC or customer notifications. Check Bluefen and other customer contracts for notification duties.
- Require a **specific indemnity** (regulatory, notification, forensic, customer claims) not subject to the basket, disclosure or Buyer knowledge, plus claims-conduct rights.

**F. Title and fundamental warranties on the same cap and time limits.**
- Reject. Title, capacity and (I'd argue) tax should be capped at 100% of the price, with no basket or de minimis and a long claim period (e.g. 6 years).
- DD-012 is the Company's own register. The Seller's letter says it is not Buyer verification. We need share certificates, executed transfers, ASIC and PPSR searches, and confirmation of no options, convertibles or encumbrances.

**G. "Limitations apply to all Claims" (cl 12.3/13) and "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).**
- As drafted, caps, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance would catch fraud, wilful concealment, specific indemnities, tax and statutory claims.
- Require express carve-outs for fraud/dishonesty, wilful concealment, title/capacity, tax, specific indemnities and covenants. Flip the drafting default so limits apply only to claims they expressly name.
- Have a litigator review the non-reliance wording against misleading-conduct claims under the ACL and Corporations Act.

**H. Disclosure and knowledge (Sch 7, DL 1.1–1.2, cl 8.3).**
- Disclosing the whole data room, "every fact, matter and circumstance contained **or referred to**", the Accounts and public registers is effectively disclosure against every warranty. Combined with cl 8.3 (constructive knowledge of anything "discoverable"), the warranties are close to worthless.
- Push for:
  - specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, with "fair" disclosure standards;
  - no disclosure of the Accounts against the accounts warranties;
  - cl 8.3 deleted or limited to actual knowledge of named individuals of specific facts;
  - an express pro-sandbagging clause;
  - an updated disclosure bring-down and no cure of breaches by post-signing disclosure.

## 3. Tier 2: need facts or drafting fixes

- **Quantifying the problem.** Riverlark, bonuses and Ironquay alone total about AUD 3.8m (about 16% of the price). If left as warranty claims, they would consume most of the AUD 4.8m cap. Deal with them through price and specific indemnities, not the warranty regime.
- **Basket and de minimis.** The basket is a deductible (excess only). Ask for a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery) and a lower de minimis with aggregation of related claims. AUD 25k per claim is high for a business with many small-ticket issues.
- **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k).** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each, which may suggest splitting to stay under an approval threshold. This is my inference and needs checking. Obtain the contracts, termination rights, approval thresholds and signing dates. Treat prepayments or accruals as debt-like, and check interim conduct covenants and leakage.
- **Tax and IP "settled".** Not accepted. We need a tax indemnity or deed running to the amendment-period horizon, and IP ownership, open-source and third-party warranties on an extended cap, since IP is the core SaaS asset.
- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Seller's wording carefully says the documents don't "state" consent is needed on a share sale. Review for deemed-assignment-on-change-of-control provisions. If there is any risk, add to the CPs or require confirmations.
- **DL para 11** ("Buyer must evaluate...") tries to shift the diligence burden to us. Reject.

## 4. Gaps worth raising

- Credit support for Seller obligations: a retention or escrow of price (e.g. through the 18-month period), or a guarantee, since Harbourglass is a holding vehicle. Consider W&I insurance as an alternative.
- Interim-period conduct covenants, a bring-down of warranties at Completion, a Material Adverse Change/termination right, and Seller non-compete and non-solicit covenants.

## 5. Summary of recommendations

1. **Don't accept "FINAL".** Verify internally what the principals agreed, and treat any agreement as covering general warranties only.
2. **Completion mechanics:** Riverlark paid out at Completion with security discharge; DD-005 bonuses and on-costs deducted from price; Ironquay paid and IP assigned before or at Completion.
3. **Bluefen:** unconditional written consent as a Buyer-only-waivable CP, with a retention or price protection as fallback.
4. **Specific indemnities:** data incident, Ironquay/IP, and the known debt-like items, all outside cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge.
5. **Fundamental, tax and IP warranties:** 100% price cap (tax and IP on extended caps), no basket, long claim period.
6. **Carve-outs** from all limitations and non-reliance for fraud, wilful concealment, title, tax and indemnities; reverse the "applies to all Claims" default.
7. **Disclosure:** specific only, fair-disclosure standard, no Accounts or public register blanket, no constructive knowledge, bring-down required.
8. **Immediate information requests:** status of the DD-006 investigation and NDB assessment, missing DL para 1.3, Sandbar contracts, Ironquay payment evidence, share transfer documents and searches, and lease and Mossvale change-of-control terms.
9. **Security:** retention or escrow (or W&I), plus interim covenants and a termination right.

I can turn this into a mark-up of clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12 and 20.5, or a Seller-facing issues list, if that would help. The privacy and ACL points should be confirmed by specialist counsel before they go to the Seller.
